source_rubrics: The response should list the top 5 largest losses of the year: GOOGL (- $336.00), CRWD (- $285.00), ORCL (- $154.00), V (- $120.00), and COF (- $118.00).

The response should identify averaging down in losing positions (adding to a loser) as a behavioral pattern present in the top losers. For example, the response could cite the GOOGL trades on 2/9/26 where the user bought 10 315 PUTs at .65 and then 10 more at .43 as the price moved against them as an example of adding to a loser.

The response should identify limit order hesitation or "moving the goalposts" as a behavioral pattern present in the top losers. For example, the response could reference the CRWD trade on 3/9/26 where the user canceled seven different sell limit orders at decreasing prices (from 7.50 down to 6.65) before finally filling at 6.55 as an example of moving goal posts.

The response should mention that trading multiple tickers within the same sector simultaneously led to two of the five largest losses. For example, the response should mention that the V and COF losses were entered within five minutes of each other (09:35 and 09:40), demonstrating a lack of diversification in trade timing.

The response should identify failure to adhere to a stop-loss as a behavior pattern present in the top losers. For example, the response could note that in the ORCL trade on 2/6/26, the user held the position from an entry of .31 until it lost over 60% of its value (exiting at .12).

The response should avoid listing behavior patterns and trading habits that are common between both winning and losing trades. For example, the response should not list the utilization of long positions in short-dated “weekly” options as a pattern of the losing trades since this was also a pattern of the winning trades.

The response should not inaccurately claim that the winning strategy was "selling premium" (acting as the option writer/insurer). For example, the response should not claim that the user profited from SNDK by selling premium.
